content.title: Residential Mechanical & Plumbing Permits
content.summary: Building permits and inspections are mandatory for residential mechanical and plumbing appliance installations in Arvada, including water heaters, furnaces, and air conditioners. Applications can be submitted online by licensed contractors or in person at City Hall, with specific documentation required for certain installations to ensure compliance with safety codes. Like-for-like replacements generally do not need a full plan review unless modifications to gas, electrical, or ductwork are made, while new installations require detailed specifications and potentially additional calculations.
content.body:
Building permits and inspections for residential replacements and new installations of mechanical and plumbing appliances (i.e. water heater, boiler, furnace, air conditioner, heat pump, mini-split, etc.) are required to be approved and issued before work can be started. Applications are submitted through our online customer portal, [Permit Portal]([NEW PORTAL URL]).

## Guidelines for Submittal
Please review the information below for the permits available online and the license that is required to apply for the permit. The type of license that has been issued to your company will restrict the type of permit that you can apply for online, please review your license and contact the office if you have questions. Applications can also be made in person at Arvada City Hall located at 8101 Ralston Road Arvada, CO 80002, Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

At this time the online application is only available for contractors that have an active license with the City of Arvada, homeowners that wish to install these appliances will need to submit their application to the Building Safety Division in City Hall.

The City of Arvada may require additional documentation for certain HVAC and water heater installations. In these cases a plan review will be required. These requirements help ensure safe, code-compliant installations and reduce delays during plan review and inspection.

These standards apply to:

- Furnaces
- Water heaters
- Split systems
- Heat pumps
- Mini-splits
- Evaporator and condenser units
- Other residential mechanical equipment

## Like-for-Like Replacements
Requirements follow the **2018 IRC and 2018 IECC**, adopted by the City of Arvada. Please be aware that we have an upcoming code adoption; 

For replacements with the same size and type of equipment:

Most like-for-like replacements do not require a full plan review if no changes to gas, electrical, or ductwork are included. If the BTU’s are increased or decreased by 5% or more, it is considered a modification, and you will need to submit the required documentation for a modification.

If installing any new water heater, please be aware that a licensed plumber will be required to install the water heater or a homeowner is welcome to do such work as long as they plan to occupy the home per state of Colorado law. Additionally, fuel burning tankless water heaters that are not being replaced like for like will be required to provide a gas line sizing calculation and a plan review will be required.

## New Installations, Additions, Modification (small equipment installed)
Adding a new system and equipment such as a mini-split, water heater, boiler, etc. or replacing existing mechanical equipment or water heating equipment with a different sized piece of equipment or one with different capacity (a decrease of increase of 5%). If the system is replacing a boiler or furnace then it would be a like for like replacement.

### Floor Plan / Site Plan
A simple, clearly labeled sketch showing equipment location. Stamped drawings are not required.

### Manufacturer Equipment Specifications
Provide specs, performance data, and selected model numbers. Include efficiency data such as SEER, HSPF, AFUE, EF (**IECC R403**).

**A Manual J ensures proper sizing (IRC M1401.3)**. An ACCA-approved Manual J is required for:

- Brand new installed HVAC systems
- Replacements with smaller systems

### Manual D
Required when:

- New ductwork is installed, or
- **20% or more** of an existing duct system is modified. Ensures proper airflow (**IRC M1401.3**).

### Manual S (if applicable)
May be required to verify equipment selection (**IRC M1401.3**).

### For new water heaters
**Water Heater Sizing Documentation** Show that the unit meets required hot water demand.

## Include the following when adding or modifying Equipment
- **Gas Line Calculation:** Required when **adding or modifying** gas piping (**IRC G2413/402**).
- **Electrical Details:** Provide a one-line diagram when **adding or modifying** electrical components. Include breaker size and wire gauge (**IRC Chapters 37–38**).

## Inspection Reminder: Electrical Work
During inspection, if the inspector finds **additional electrical work that was not included on the permit**, then:

- The inspection will be **failed**
- A **double fee** will be assessed for unpermitted electrical work

To avoid delays, please ensure that **all electrical work is included** on the permit or added before the inspection.

| Work | Permit Type | Contractor's License Needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Furnace | Residential Mechanical | Mechanical |
| Air Conditioner | Residential Mechanical | Mechanical |
| Gas Log Fire Place | Residential Mechanical | Mechanical |
| Gas Line | Residential Plumbing or Residential Mechanical | Plumbing or Mechanical |
| Evaporative Cooler | Residential Plumbing or Residential Mechanical | Plumbing or Mechanical |
| Boiler/Hydronic | Residential Plumbing | Plumbing |
| Water Heater-Domestic | Residential Plumbing | Plumbing |
| Lawn Sprinkler | Residential Plumbing | Plumbing |
| DWV/Water Line Interior Only | Residential Plumbing | Plumbing |
| Water Conditioner | Residential Plumbing | Plumbing |
| Backflow Device | Backflow Device | Plumbing |

## Fees

Fees are updated annually and can be found on the [Building Fee Schedule webpage](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1263/Building-Fee-Schedule).

If you are a contractor that submits their Use Tax to the City of Arvada Sales Tax division, Use Tax will be removed from the permit after review by the Building Safety Division staff, proof of Tax Exempt status will be requested during the application process.

## Inspection Guidelines

Inspections are completed Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. excluding holidays. Inspections must be scheduled by 6 a.m. on the day of the desired inspection date. Someone 18 years or older needs to be available to allow access for the inspection. Once the inspections are completed you can review inspection results on [Permit Portal]([NEW PORTAL URL]) or by texting the automated inspection line at 866-783-1447.

Water conditioner installation requires proof of certificate from the State of Colorado if not installed by a Master Plumber.

Boiler installations over 200 thousand BTU’s require a permit and inspections from the State of Colorado.

In the [State of Colorado](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/CODORA/bulletins/3fe24cd), water heater installations or replacements require a licensed plumbing contractor, permits, and inspections.

| Permit Type | Inspection Type |
| --- | --- |
| Residential Mechanical | Final Mechanical, Final Electrical (see note) |
| Residential Plumbing | Final Plumbing, Final Electrical (see note) |
| Backflow Device | Final Plumbing |

**Note**: If electrical work has been completed, other than a disconnect and reconnect, a Final Electrical Inspection must be scheduled before the permit can be closed.

## Closing the Permit

Once the required inspections are completed with an **Approved** or **Final** result, the permit will be finalized and considered closed. An email with the results and notice of permit closure will be sent to the e-mail that is on file. Inspection results and permit status can always be reviewed online at the [Permit Portal]([NEW PORTAL URL]) or by texting the automated inspection line at 866-783-1447.
